record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: For every cubic planar graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G, is it always possible to choose three pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings, meaning three proper colorings from the same lists that assign mutually different colors to each vertex?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4 Is it possible to choose three disjoint proper colourings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a cubic planar graph (a 3-regular graph that can be embedded in the plane) and let $L$ be a list assignment that assigns to each vertex $v \in V(G)$ a set $L(v)$ of three colors. A proper $L$-coloring of $G$ is a function $c$ such that $c(v) \in L(v)$ for every vertex $v$ and $c(u) \neq c(v)$ for every edge $uv \in E(G)$. Two proper $L$-colorings $c_1$ and $c_2$ are called disjoint if $c_1(v) \neq c_2(v)$ for every vertex $v \in V(G)$.

Is it true that for every cubic planar graph $G$ and every 3-list-assignment $L$ of $G$, there exist three pairwise disjoint proper $L$-colorings of $G$ (that is, three proper $L$-colorings $c_1, c_2, c_3$ such that for each vertex $v$, the values $c_1(v), c_2(v), c_3(v)$ are three distinct colors)?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on list packing numbers of planar graphs (e.g., Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Davies–Kang, 2023) studies disjoint list-colorings under girth constraints but does not resolve the cubic planar case. No published proof or counterexample for the specific question on cubic planar graphs with 3-list-assignments was found; the problem is posed as an open question at a recent workshop on cycles and colourings.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Lowers the two-times-degeneracy upper bound for the list packing number of planar graphs of girth 3, 4 or 5; proves results on disjoint L-colorings under girth conditions but does not settle the cubic planar case.
status_evidence.claim: The cubic planar 3-list packing problem is not resolved by current planar list-packing results.

status_evidence.title: Counting Packings of List-colorings of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses list packing numbers and disjoint proper list-colorings; cubic planar 3-list packing not established.
status_evidence.claim: No known proof that cubic planar graphs admit three pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings for every 3-list-assignment.
